letters.fact: Count from 1 all the way up, connecting each dot in order, and a capital A appears — great practice matching numbers to the shape of a letter.
Follow the numbers around the two rounded bumps of the letter B — a fun curved path to trace with a pencil or crayon.
C is one open curve, so the dot path sweeps smoothly from the top all the way around to the bottom — an easy one for beginners.
D pairs a straight edge with one big curve, so little ones practice switching between a ruler-straight line and a smooth arc.
E has three straight arms, so the dot-to-dot path doubles back across the middle — good practice picking the pencil up and placing it back down.
F is one of the simplest connect-the-dots shapes here — just two arms off a single tall stem.
G curls almost all the way around like a C, then tucks in with a small hook — a satisfying shape to complete.
H is two straight towers joined by a bridge, so the dot path jumps across the middle before finishing the second side.
The tall stem of I is dotted first, then one extra numbered dot sits above it for the tittle — a neat example of a letter with a floating dot of its own.
J hooks at the bottom like a fishing hook, with a separate numbered dot marking the top just like the letter I.
K has two diagonal legs meeting a straight spine, so the connect-the-dots path angles sharply partway through.
L is about as simple as connect-the-dots gets — one long straight line down, one short line across.
M has two tall peaks and a valley in the middle, so the dot path zig-zags before finishing the second tower — one of the more detailed letters here.
N takes a diagonal shortcut between two straight towers — a nice letter for practicing straight-line control.
O is a single smooth loop, so every dot sits evenly around the ring — trace it slowly for a perfect circle.
P is a straight stem with one rounded loop at the top — like tracing half of a B.
Q is a circle with a little tail kicking out at the bottom corner — watch for the extra dots that finish the tail.
R combines a straight stem, a rounded loop, and a kicking leg — one of the more detailed letters to connect.
S curves back and forth in one continuous line, so the dot-to-dot path snakes smoothly from top to bottom.
T is a short top bar and a single stem — a quick, confidence-building connect-the-dots for younger kids.
U is a rounded cup shape, so the dot path curves gently down and back up between two straight sides.
V is two diagonal lines meeting in a sharp point — good practice for straight, angled pencil strokes.
W doubles the zig-zag of a V, with two sharp points across the bottom — one of the most detailed capital letters to trace here.
X crosses two diagonal lines, so the numbered path has to double back through the middle to finish both strokes.
Y branches into two arms up top before joining into one stem — the dot path splits just like the letter's shape.
Z zig-zags in three straight strokes, so the dot-to-dot path changes direction sharply twice.
